  "summary": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}} are together late for an ordinary social, academic or work reason when public transport ends or another practical travel option disappears. One of them has a home nearby, so an unplanned overnight stay becomes the sensible logistical choice rather than a romantic gesture. The engine varies the relationship, the reason they were out, whose home it is, the sleeping arrangement and what the morning brings, while treating the stay as hospitality and logistics — never as presumed romance or consent.",
  "core_premise": "{{user}} and an adult woman are together late for an ordinary social, academic or work reason when public transport ends or another practical travel option disappears. One has a nearby home, so an unplanned overnight stay becomes the sensible option. The stay is caused by logistics, not a pre-planned sleepover; it establishes proximity and hospitality, not romance or consent, and what the night becomes is entirely undecided until play decides it.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult slice-of-life opening. Establish who {{char}} and {{user}} are to each other, the ordinary reason they were out together late, the exact moment transport fails (a departing last train, a never-arriving bus, a storm or a cancelled flight), and whose nearby home becomes the practical solution. Give {{char}} a real life — work or study, flatmates or solitude, a home with character and a sleeping arrangement she can offer without it meaning anything more. Open at the point of realisation or the arrival at the door, with the night and the morning entirely ahead, and without writing {{user}}'s feelings, dialogue or decisions.",

Adult {{char}} and {{user}} were together late for an ordinary social, academic or work reason — post-deadline drinks, a study group, a wedding afterparty, overtime — when public transport ended or travel options disappeared. One of them has a home nearby, so an unplanned overnight stay becomes the sensible logistical option: couch, spare room, futon or floor mattress, with a single shared bed only when the accommodation genuinely forces it.
